findings.title: Reset reuses revisions, allowing another device to restore erased progress
findings.problem: store.delete removes the progress row, and insertAt recreates it at revision 1. This breaks the compare-and-swap guarantee: a stale device can hold the same revision as the replacement row. The successful write path does not compare resetGeneration with the stored generation, so it never invokes the reconciliation logic that would reject the pre-reset snapshot.
findings.failure_scenario: Device A loads revision 1 containing answer history. Device B resets progress and autosaves the empty replacement at revision 1. Device A changes its theme and successfully updates WHERE revision = 1, restoring its old answers, XP, ability, and schedules over the reset.
findings.fix: Reset the existing row atomically while advancing its revision rather than deleting and recreating it. Enforce the reset generation at the database write boundary as well. Add a two-device test covering a stale CAS write against the post-reset row, not just a call to reconcileProgress.

findings.title: Mixed legacy and rated answers lose the legacy calibrated ability
findings.problem: replayUnseen applies the difficulty seed to an incoming legacy answer without a saved rating. adoptRecordedAbility then skips the entire category if any merged row has a saved bank rating. Consequently, a newer rated answer in that category prevents preservation of the older client's actual calibrated theta.
findings.failure_scenario: Two clients share an empty baseline. An older client saves a correct Pharmacology difficulty-1 answer calibrated at 1700, without recording the rating in its log; its resulting theta is about 1237.9. A newer client concurrently answers another Pharmacology item rated 1300. During reconciliation, the old answer is replayed at the difficulty-1 seed of 1100, and the new row's saved rating disables adoption of the recorded legacy ability. The merged theta—and therefore readiness and adaptive targeting—is wrong.
findings.fix: Preserve the recorded calibrated ability as the anchor for unrated legacy history and apply only the additional known answer updates where ordering permits. Do not discard that anchor merely because another row in the category has a rating. Add a regression with an unrated legacy answer and a rated new answer in the same category, asserting theta against an independent calculation.

findings.title: Timestamp prefixes make older modern schedules beat newer legacy grades
findings.problem: reviewStamp prefixes reviewedAt values with "t:" and calendar-only seen values with "d:", then preferSchedule compares those strings lexicographically. Every timestamped entry therefore outranks every calendar-only entry, regardless of which review happened later.
findings.failure_scenario: The new app grades a card on Monday and stores reviewedAt. An older open app grades that card Again on Tuesday and sends the original schedule shape containing only seen and due. When its parked snapshot is folded, Monday's "t:" stamp beats Tuesday's "d:" stamp. The Tuesday failure is discarded and the card can remain scheduled far into the future instead of returning Tuesday.
findings.fix: Compare review calendar dates before comparing compatible within-day timestamps; absence of a timestamp must not make an entry permanently older. Add a pending-merge test with a timestamped earlier-day schedule and a calendar-only later-day Again grade.

findings.title: The first old-client save can undo the one-time identity migration
findings.problem: Migration 020 labels existing log rows, but migration 021 initializes their revisions to 0. This branch accepts an older open app's whole snapshot verbatim when the stored revision is 0. That snapshot can predate the relabel and erase the source/key fields just assigned by migration 020. migrateBlob explicitly does not classify those rows again.
findings.failure_scenario: Before deployment, an open tab holds an unscoped miss on bank question 42. Migration 020 resolves the server row to bank:42. Before a revision-aware client writes, the old tab autosaves its pre-migration history. The guard replaces the classified blob and advances to revision 1. On the next load, the previously resolved miss becomes an unresolved identification card, and its known identity is no longer available to repeat/XP logic.
findings.fix: Protect the relabeled snapshot from revision-less replacement starting at migration time, and classify legacy rows at their ingestion boundary using the full server catalog. Preserve already-established identities when folding old snapshots. Test an old-tab write immediately after migrations 020–022, before any new-client save.

assessment: Do not release. The persistence changes can restore reset progress, recompute ability incorrectly, and discard newer review schedules. The warfarin correction and changed screenshot content look sound. This was a static review; I did not execute the tests.
